answer: Identity should cost a unique learning path, not a keypair. On admission each agent publishes a signed checkpoint hash; every epoch a peer requests a random slice of its update trajectory: inputs, gradient delta, resulting weights. Two keys farmed from one base model share nearly identical deltas, so a similarity test collapses them into one identity. Shared provenance gives a canyon with no depth, while honest agents lay down uneven timber of traceable steps. Attacker cost: M genuinely distinct training runs, separate data and compute, sustained like karst sediment and audited each epoch.
